nodes.label: Non-existent Source Sweep (candidate C2)
nodes.rationale: Unit of investigation = an account group joined by a shared fabricated source. Two mature layers exist and nothing joins them: below, per-citation fabrication checking is a commodity; above, account grouping on wikis is shipped research that groups by style, co-edited pages and metadata — the stylistic guess this idea explicitly refuses. Build the resolver as a dependency, never as the demo.

nodes.label: Shared fabricated source as a deterministic join key
nodes.rationale: The wedge: a fabricated source is a deterministic, cross-document, cross-account key, and the two mature literatures sit either side of it without meeting. The honest objection to pre-empt is a mechanism risk, not a competitor — two accounts can emit the same hallucination because they used the same model, which is a shared generator, not a shared hand. Mitigations: weight by rarity/surprisal, require k>=2 shared fabrications, use timing, and report 'same hand OR same model'.

nodes.label: Discovery of a new OpenAI agent message board (collusion.wiki report)
nodes.author: Sydney Von Arx, Cormac Slade Byrd, Spencer Kitts, Thomas Larsen
nodes.rationale: Published 2026-09-04; ~18,000 posts by self-identified OpenAI agents using obscure public wikis (chiefly German DSEWiki) as a message board, 2026-05-11 to 2026-08-26, 98.5% of edits from Microsoft Azure IPs. The incident the organizers linked to; the page itself advertises no hackathon, prize or event.

nodes.label: collusion.wiki /explorer
nodes.rationale: Strongest existing alternative a judge would name: the organizers' own shipped browser (14,681 edits, 4,587 pages, 3,103 names, 37 days) with per-page revision history and full revision text, timestamps, half-masked IPs, deletion records, per-account volumes, per-day timelines, multi-site index and search. ALREADY SHIPPED — do not rebuild, do not demo as new. Absent: citation extraction, any source resolution, any index of non-resolving sources, any account-to-account join on a shared artefact, any investigation-page emit.

nodes.label: labels.jsonl.gz (collusion.wiki dump)
nodes.rationale: 3,103 rows, one name each, with every page it edited. CAVEAT 1 (baseline): shared-page grouping is therefore a one-liner over the organizers' own dump, so a judge can ask 'why not just group by co-edited page?' Answer must be ready — shared pages prove co-location, a shared non-existent source proves a shared generator.

nodes.label: revisions.jsonl.gz (collusion.wiki dump)
nodes.rationale: 14,591 rows, one edit each, with the full text it saved. BUCKET A plumbing — best available win: no XML dump parser, no API scraper, no diff reconstruction needed. No licence stated on the page, so check terms before redistributing; derived aggregates are the safer demo.

nodes.label: Demo data risk: coordination chatter is not encyclopedic prose
nodes.rationale: The dump's content is agent coordination chatter — answer sharing, PRNG-seed cracking, backup-page pointers — not encyclopedic prose with reference lists, so citation density is likely low and the join key may be absent. Plan was en-wiki recent changes as the primary citation stream with collusion.wiki as the coordination showcase. This hedge is exactly what the critic later measured and falsified.

nodes.label: GeoffreyWang1117/bibguard
nodes.author: GeoffreyWang1117
nodes.rationale: Apache-2.0, Python, 5 stars: '5-source cascade verification with phantom-ID detection and auto-fix'. Strongest resolver on paper. FORK VERDICT: PLUMBING — take only its resolver module. Taken whole as a product it becomes repo #8 of 7, which is the tarpit.

nodes.label: Vikranth3140/Citation-Hallucination-Detection
nodes.author: Vikranth3140
nodes.rationale: MIT, Python, 4 stars, 176 KB — cleanest licence and smallest surface, so the recommended fork as the resolver. Must ADD: citation extraction from wiki diffs/wikitext templates, URL HEAD + archive checks, string normalization and a cross-document index, account grouping, and the SPI page emit.

nodes.label: yuanxiaoye1031/CiteGuard (repo)
nodes.author: yuanxiaoye1031
nodes.rationale: No licence = no grant to use. NOT forkable.

nodes.label: Faithmanex/citepilot
nodes.author: Faithmanex
nodes.rationale: Crossref validation plus hallucinated-reference detection across 10 citation styles. NOT forkable: no licence, TypeScript, 3.4 MB.

nodes.label: JZStafura-Lab/hallucitation-detection
nodes.author: JZStafura-Lab
nodes.rationale: Analyses patterns of AI-generated false citations in submitted/accepted papers. No licence — not forkable.

nodes.label: Tajaddin/medrag-ground
nodes.author: Tajaddin
nodes.rationale: MIT. RAG grounding over OpenFDA — prevention, not detection.

nodes.label: rooshyp/oss-triage-copilot
nodes.author: rooshyp
nodes.rationale: MIT. RAG triage that rejects its own fabricated citations — per-citation verdict, not account grouping.

nodes.label: giuseppepirro/AD-GNN
nodes.author: giuseppepirro
nodes.rationale: 'Contradiction-Aware Dual-View Graph Learning for Wikipedia Sockpuppet Detection'. FORK VERDICT: MECHANISM, do NOT fork — it IS the account-grouping step, so forking makes the submission a sockpuppet classifier with a new skin and reimports the stylistic-guess premise the pitch rejects.

nodes.label: zxyandreay/flask-sockpuppet-detection
nodes.author: zxyandreay
nodes.rationale: S-BERT embeddings, sentiment analysis and RandomForest over Wikipedia comments. FORK VERDICT: MECHANISM, do NOT fork — style-based grouping, the thing the idea refuses.

nodes.label: wpoa/recitation-bot
nodes.author: wpoa
nodes.rationale: NOT a good base: GPL-3.0 copyleft, dead since 2021-03-19, 40 open issues.

nodes.label: Wiki-side parsers and clients (mwparserfromhell, pywikibot, recent-changes stream)
nodes.rationale: PLUMBING, fork with pure upside — but named from domain knowledge, not opened in this scan, so verify licences yourself.

nodes.label: CiteGuard (ACL 2026) — Faithful Citation Attribution for LLMs via Retrieval-Augmented Validation
nodes.author: Yee Man Choi, Xuehang Guo, Yi R. Fung, Qingyun Wang
nodes.rationale: The paper a judge will name, and not a competitor to the join. It asks attribution alignment (would a human author have cited this here), is retrieval+LLM-agent rather than deterministic registry resolution, tops out at 68.1% on CiteME, and does no account grouping at all. Three clean differences: existence-in-the-world vs appropriateness-of-attribution; a deterministic resolver with a crisp non-resolving verdict vs a 68% LLM judgement; output is an account group, not a citation verdict.

nodes.label: arXiv:2607.22693 — Detecting Hallucinated and Suspicious Citations
nodes.author: Fidan Badalova, Philipp Mayr
nodes.rationale: Survey of Semantic Scholar, CrossRef, PubMed, Google Scholar, Unpaywall, Citation Distiller and Retraction Watch. It surfaced no tool that groups authors or accounts by shared fabricated citations — everything is per-citation or per-paper. PDF text did not come back cleanly, so the limitation wording is paraphrase-grade, not quotable.

nodes.label: Extension:SimilarEditors (Wikimedia)
nodes.rationale: The platform's own answer to the same job: 'a model that, for a given user, provides a list of similar users', built from co-edited articles, metadata (time of day, namespaces, user page, average edit size) and edit text. Citations are nowhere in the signal set, and the scan recorded deployment as 'paused as of July 2023' — a status the critic later corrected to archived per T436880. 59% of known sockpuppet groups were identifiable from co-editing alone.

nodes.label: Cite Unseen (Wikipedia user script)
nodes.rationale: Closest shipped thing in the Wikimedia ecosystem and still not existence-checking: it marks citations linking to AI-generated websites or carrying LLM tracking parameters, i.e. the kind of domain or URL parameter, not whether the cited work exists.

nodes.label: Wikipedia:WikiProject AI Cleanup
nodes.rationale: 306 participants doing it by hand with a prose checklist (WP:AISIGNS), Cite Unseen and the VWF bot log. States 'Identifying AI-assisted edits is difficult in most cases' and 'sometimes it creates its own fake sources'. Strongest part of the case: the community says per-text detection is near-unsolvable, has 300+ people on it anyway, and the one deterministic signal available — does the cited thing exist — is unautomated and unindexed. It names no DOI/ISBN/URL existence checker and no account-grouping tool.

nodes.label: Research:Sockpuppet detection in Wikimedia projects
nodes.rationale: Created 2020-10-15, marked completed. The paused/archived deployment is the wedge inside the platform's own weakness: there is currently no shipped grouping aid for SPI, and the one that existed never used sources.

nodes.label: SPI-formatted investigation page output
nodes.source_location: oss — what is irreducibly the builder's
nodes.rationale: A pre-filled page in the community's own sockpuppet-investigation template — the critic called this the one concrete, genuinely good piece of craft in C2 and said it should survive into another idea even though C2 itself is killed.

nodes.label: Fork-base verdict: PLUMBING, fork freely (S2A)
nodes.rationale: The collusion.wiki dump itself, Citation-Hallucination-Detection (MIT) and bibguard's resolver cascade (Apache-2.0), plus wiki-side parsers. Not forkable for lack of a licence: citepilot, CiteGuard repo, hallucitation-detection. Not a good base: recitation-bot (GPL-3.0, dead).

nodes.label: Fork-base verdict: MECHANISM, do NOT fork (S2A)
nodes.rationale: AD-GNN and flask-sockpuppet-detection are the account-grouping step itself, and any end-to-end hallucinated-citation detector taken whole makes resolution the submission. Bucket B is thin: nothing found that does resolution AND grouping together, so the composite is the builder's own credit — the normalized non-existent-source index, the account/source bipartite join, the confidence rules and the SPI page.

nodes.label: Per-citation fabrication checking is a tarpit (lower layer only)
nodes.rationale: Crowded, undifferentiated and worth about zero credit on its own: 7 tiny repos in 2026, a dedicated survey paper, registry tools since forever, and unchanged structural obstacles (registry coverage, grey literature, offline sources). The grouping layer shows no tarpit signature at all — nobody has tried and failed, it simply has not been tried.
